verdict.rationale: Visa Intelligent Commerce documents its own spend controls. Purchase-intent mandates carry a required declineThreshold amount and an effectiveUntilTime expiry, and the platform enforces network-level controls so credentials and authorizations match the authenticated instruction. Revocation is documented only as an agent cancelling a purchase intent, and agent token 'life cycle management' is mentioned without any explicit token-revocation capability. Caps are scoped per instruction or mandate rather than as standing per-agent limits, and the product is flagged as still in development. Missing for 10: standing per-agent caps and usage limits beyond per-mandate thresholds, a documented instant revocation of an agent's token or payment authority, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set per-agent spend caps and usage limits and revoke an agent's payment authority instantly

citations.quote: Capture consumer consent, set spending limits, and manage mandates for agent-initiated payments.
Your agent can cancel a purchase intent when the customer chooses to not make the purchase.
The Visa Intelligent Commerce platform will validate that these requests match the authenticated user instruction and set network level controls.
Provisioning and life cycle management of agent-specific payment tokens that can be used by agents to make secure transactions on behalf of the user
